speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-infectious bronchial hyperreactivity (cough-variant asthma) or reactive airway disease.

While the patient mentions a "Pyelonephritis" diagnosis from a previous visit, that condition affects the kidneys and does not cause respiratory symptoms like cough and shortness of breath triggered by exertion. Given the recent upper respiratory infection and the nature of your symptoms, I suspect the infection may have triggered an airway sensitivity issue. I will need to see the Chest X-Ray results to rule out pneumonia or other structural issues before we can confirm this.
